reviews.text: Good story, well told, didn't keep me up past midnight. The interviews are the best part -- each suspect has their own way of dodging and you can feel the old secret underneath. Voigt's confession is strong. But the mystery itself isn't much of a mystery; you've a fair idea who did it before the halfway mark. And the ending is too quiet for my taste. Rain and coffee. Grand for a literary magazine, maybe, but I wanted the story to land a punch it never quite throws.
